deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost blank. It holds only a few short jottings at the top. The faint text visible lower down is show-through from the verso/adjacent leaf and is not part of this page. The archival pencil heading 'Riemann 3' and the folio number '35' are later additions.

Content, row by row:

(i) Two triples of factors in Greek letters: 1/(1-βγ), 1/(1-αγ), 1/(1-αβ), and the primed copy 1/(1-β'γ'), 1/(1-α'γ'), 1/(1-α'β').

(ii) The same pattern in Latin letters: 1/(1-a), 1/(1-b), 1/(1-c) and 1/(1-a'), 1/(1-b'), 1/(1-c'). This suggests the abbreviation a=βγ, b=αγ, c=αβ (and similarly primed). That reading is my inference, not written on the page.

(iii) Three expressions: -b-c+bc, -a-c+ac (Riemann first wrote 'ba', struck it out and wrote 'ac'), and -a-b+ab. These are exactly (1-b)(1-c)-1, (1-a)(1-c)-1 and (1-a)(1-b)-1. So he was expanding pairwise products of the denominators. For example, 1/((1-b)(1-c)) = 1/(1+(-b-c+bc)). This interpretation is mine.

(iv) The full product of six factors 1/(1-a)·1/(1-b)·1/(1-c)·1/(1-a')·1/(1-b')·1/(1-c'), followed by the monomial abc·a'b'c'. Possibly he is looking at the leading term or a normalisation of the product, or factoring out abc·a'b'c'.

(v) The reciprocals 1/(a+bc), 1/(b+ac), 1/(c+ab), plus the primed denominators a'+b'c', b'+a'c', c'+a'b'. Two or three further small fractions to the right (something like 1/(bc), 1/(ac)) are struck out.

The forms a+bc, b+ac, c+ab arise naturally from the substitution a=βγ, b=αγ, c=αβ. For instance a+bc = βγ + α²βγ = βγ(1+α²). So these may be an attempt to symmetrise or factor a product of rational functions in three variables. However, the page gives no derivation, no equation and no stated purpose.

Connection to the bundle: the neighbouring pages (Riemann's ξ/ζ computations, Gauss/Jacobi-sum products φ(ρ,α^r)φ(ρ,α^s), theta transformations) do not visibly use these expressions. Any link, e.g. to a product of geometric series, a generating function, or Jacobi-sum manipulation, is speculative. Riemann's purpose cannot be determined from this page.
errors: No errors detectable: the only checkable content is the identity (1-b)(1-c) = 1-b-c+bc and its permutations, which is correct. Riemann's correction 'ba' to 'ac' in the second expression is the right one.

results.what: Expansion of pairwise products of denominators: (1-b)(1-c)-1 = -b-c+bc, etc., and the companion expressions a+bc, b+ac, c+ab (and primed versions)
results.modern_name: elementary algebraic manipulation of rational functions in three variables (scratch work)

transcription_corrections: The heading 'Riemann 3' is a later archival pencil annotation, not Riemann's hand; likewise the folio number '35' and the mark 'x' at upper right.
Second expression: Riemann wrote '-a-c+ba', struck 'ba' and wrote 'ac'. The transcription's [-ba-]{+ac+} is correct in substance.
The small fractions to the right of 1/(a+bc) 1/(b+ac) 1/(c+ab), and to the right of c'+a'b', are struck out and largely illegible. 'bc', 'ac' are plausible but uncertain readings.
The faint material lower on the page (numbers, formulas) is show-through from the other side of the leaf and should not be transcribed as content of 35r.
